reviews.text: Competent and very helpful staff.
Very positive experience!!

A center of excellence!!!
We went to the CVS Specialized Veterinary Center in Rome to have our guinea pig examined, and we couldn't have found a better place!
From the moment we were welcomed, we sensed great professionalism and sensitivity. Not all vets have experience with exotic animals, but here we found truly specialized doctors who examined our little one with incredible care and expertise.
They explained everything to us calmly, without rushing, answering all our questions and giving us valuable advice on his diet and daily care.
You can tell they truly love animals!!!
The center is spotless, organized, and super-equipped.
Thank you so much to all the CVS staff for treating our little guinea pig...like a member of the family! We felt right at home!!!
Highly recommended to anyone with an unconventional pet and looking for true specialists in Rome!
Always the best ❤️

Whatever review I might write, words would never be enough to thank Dr. Selleri's clinic for the care, professionalism, and promptness with which they cared for my little bunny. I obviously thank Dr. Selleri and I sincerely thank Dr. Masi for his compassion and for the excellent treatment he provided for my little bunny, Francis. I also thank Dr. Cecilia for her patience. I came from Perugia because I knew I'd find the best, and I found the best. Whatever animal you have and want to bring it to a safe place, then yes, you've come to the right place. Thank you from the bottom of my heart, Giovanni, Imane, and little Francis.

We wish to express our deepest gratitude to Dr. Andrea De Dominicis and the entire staff at the Centro Veterinario Specialistico in Roma Nomentana. On September 8th, after two days of hospitalization, our 12-year-old Westie Dominic left us to finally run free of all pain in the meadows of paradise. In such a dark and painful moment, marked by the knowledge of his imminent departure, my wife and I found in Dr. De Dominicis not only an extremely attentive professional, but also a person of extraordinary sensitivity, empathy, and compassion. He treated Dominic's grave situation with unparalleled dedication and compassion, simultaneously comforting and assisting us at every moment. Thank you from the bottom of our hearts, Dr. De Dominicis, for caring for our beloved Dominic until his last moment, and for us as well, with such heartfelt respect and understanding for our grief. You certainly do credit to the veterinary profession!
Just hope your pets don't get sick on Sundays, otherwise it'll be a BLAST! 🤑💸💸 …

They currently have the best oncologist and diagnostician in Rome. And also one of the best ophthalmologists.
The clinic is quite convenient thanks to the parking lot. The front desk staff is very friendly.

If I could give a 0, I would! A cold and superficial welcome in a facility where a long-haired professional, whose role I don't even know since she didn't introduce herself, didn't even welcome me inside and, at the front door, dismissed me in five seconds, talking only about dead dogs and referring me to a neurologist, without even listening to the fact that the problem had arisen after taking the wrong medication. Fortunately, by going elsewhere and without a neurologist, I was welcomed by competent people who immediately understood the cause, stopped the medication, started therapy, and made my little dog feel better the very next day.
but also no...
Punctual and efficient ophthalmology department
I highly recommend this property to everyone.

We turned to this clinic today, Sunday, September 13th, after contacting so many scavengers. We had an elderly cat in the terminal stages of cancer, so we weren't expecting miracles, but rather humane help for a loving cat who was about to be put to sleep. We waited our turn because there are so many animal lovers in need, and many were in the waiting room waiting for help. We will never forget the help you gave us, her owners, especially in a humane way, as we sought a solution to stop our elderly furry friend from suffering any longer. We thank Dr. Antonella and Dr. Luca Ciavatta immensely.
We will never forget you, and from now on, we can only speak highly of you. Thank you for the people you are. Stefania & Ruggero

Second lovebird I've brought to this clinic and second parakeet to die.
The first one was given too high a dose of a medication and the next day the parakeet died.
The second one... he came into the clinic with epileptic seizures, almost dead after 4 days... his head was shaking, more dazed than ever... I felt like crying... he died after 6 hours... the doctor, after 4 days of hospitalization, didn't even bother to turn around and say hello... THEY DID EXPERIMENT ON HIM... LET'S CHANGE THE DRUG AND SEE...

EXCELLENT CLINIC....OF COURSE...
YOU DON'T UNDERSTAND MUCH ABOUT EXOTIC FOODS...
Good morning Roberto, thanks for your review. If you don't mind, can I ask you what you didn't like so much or what we could do to improve and reach five stars?

My husband and I went to this wonderful clinic with the utmost urgency for our dwarf lop rabbit Linus after promptly giving us an appointment the same afternoon of the call.. From the very beginning, both the administration and the doctor who examined and treated him were very friendly.. You could feel, in addition to a lot of competence and professionalism, the love, passion and dedication for their job and the animals.. It really amazed us, having left him hospitalized one night, how at each stage of the visits and blood tests they informed us by telephone also updating us on his health status (if he had eaten, made balls, mood etc.) .. in addition, the clinic is equipped with machinery including the new generation MRI.. at the time of discharge they recounted the whole summary and explained what to do next, also giving us the prescribed medicines and being able to purchase Criticum as an alternative diet in case he had not eaten after the anesthesia and the operation, thus also freeing us from the inconvenience of going to look for them late in the evening and allowing us to start the treatment from the following morning.. we highly recommend it and all the staff, including the administration, are really kind, friendly, explanatory and transparent even in making a quote right away without any surprises at the time of payment.. thank you so much for taking care of our love Linus ❤️

My experience at this clinic wasn't at all positive. I took my dog ​​to the emergency room because it was a Saturday in late August and my vet wasn't available. After a two-hour wait, they examined her. I should point out that I was the only one in the waiting room, but
there was a lot of people coming and going in the clinic, perhaps private consultations. My dog ​​didn't have any serious symptoms, so I waited patiently. When we finally entered, I found a doctor who wasn't at all empathetic, neither with me nor with the dog. Despite never having bitten anyone, either playfully or seriously, she was treated like a dog that needed to be muzzled. Luckily, she's a very gentle dog and didn't make a sound, nor did I object to the vet's decision. After consulting a colleague, she gave me her diagnosis: Malassezia. I left hesitantly, because during the initial examination of her ear, she had suspected the presence of a foxtail. After 10 days of treatment, I'm taking my dog ​​back for a checkup, but this time at my trusted clinic. My dog ​​didn't have malassezia, but a foxtail that had been stuck in her ear for over 10 days. And what's more, they removed it without anesthesia, even though it was deep inside. Now, assuming everyone makes mistakes, I don't think I'll ever set foot in this emergency room again, because confusing a foxtail with an ear infection seems excessive. Not to mention the hefty bill I had to pay for hearing such nonsense. It's a shame, because it was right next door.
Excellent specialist center, attentive, scrupulous and welcoming staff.

You can't give an injectable treatment to a fish, say "Call me if you have any problems, we're close by," and then not respond for two days, after which the fish dies... and be told, "It's just a fish, after all!" What kind of job do you do?
And the results of the tests I paid for never arrived!
If I could have given 0 stars, I would have! Dishonest and inhumane!

I was pleasantly surprised by this clinic, even though I had my prejudices about clinics based on past experiences. My vets recommended it to me for an emergency, and I must say that it will remain a welcome point of reference, should the need arise, and I can even recommend it.

My contact person within the facility is... Dr. C. Maniscalco! I will soon also test the facility as the cat I care for, ex-colony, FIV+, will also need to undergo CMR and perhaps undergo surgery at the facility. I have faith in the facility.
Arrived on a Saturday for an emergency. Despite the crowds, they managed to take care of the dog with incredible kindness and skill. Highly recommended.

Months later, I feel compelled to share my unpleasant experience, which doesn't focus on the medical aspect because, unfortunately, I don't have the expertise (although today the doubt that my dog ​​could have been saved is more acute than ever), but on the human aspect.
One evening, my dog ​​started having trouble breathing. I immediately went to the emergency room, but the next morning she passed away.
A few days later, my cat also began to feel ill, and I took him there as well. As soon as I arrived, the lady at the counter asked me if I was there for my dog, then said, "Oh no, she's dead." Well, thanks for the kindness. But the worst part came in the following days. When I was downstairs during visiting hours, spending time with my cat, I heard two doctors, holding a small dog in their arms, say, "We have to be careful, we have the future of the clinic in our arms."
It's sadly obvious that there are first-class patients and second-class patients, as in any context, but it would be appropriate not to make it known so publicly. I don't want to go into the merits of this statement now, partly because I hope I've misinterpreted it, but honestly, certain things just can't be tolerated, especially in front of clients who are facing unpleasant situations and paying dearly for these services. So I certainly don't have the expertise to determine whether or not they did everything possible to save my dog, but they've definitely lost my trust.
Highly recommended!!!!!!!

Great experience
Very good and kind
I took my cat for surgery to remove a cyst. The reception was excellent and professional, with plenty of explanations on what to do while my cat was at home. Excellent.
Top professionalism and competence
Great! Fast and respectful. I went because my dog ​​may have swallowed a battery. We had the x-ray done in a few minutes. The price was reasonable, including the consultation.

The experience was definitely positive. Thanks above all to the professionalism, helpfulness, and kindness of Dr. Martina Confaloni, who cared for my dog, demonstrating not only expertise but also great sensitivity and compassion. Otherwise, the facility, especially the waiting room, requires maintenance and modernization.
A positive note also goes to the reception staff, who were always helpful and understanding.
I was truly impressed by the kindness and professionalism of Dr. Freri.

I visited this clinic for the first time, bringing my African grey parrot.
Excellent welcome, staff, and services.
Well done and congratulations!
Echocardiography of a Pitbull-like dog. Friendly staff and very thorough examination, on time. Excellent.
Excellent veterinary facility, welcoming staff and truly trained specialists, highly recommended
Friendly and animal-friendly staff. Professional and knowledgeable veterinarians, a leader in veterinary ophthalmology and beyond.

They don't answer their phone, emails, or WhatsApp messages, and the medical director is unreachable. I've paid CVS approximately €6,000 for 2025 alone. I'll never forget the time I had an appointment with a veterinarian, and when I arrived at the front desk, a receptionist who was supposed to notify the vet of my arrival replied, "If I see her, I'll let her know," without moving from her seat. The level of professionalism in healthcare services is completely unacceptable!
Dr. Adolfo Guandalini and his team were exceptional
Hospitality, sensitivity, competence, great professionalism, use of cutting-edge techniques.
Very professional and kind 🐾🐾🐶 …

Professionalism...
Passion
Courtesy
Clean
Courteous and helpful staff, above all very competent

The feeling is that of a service where you pay for individual services, but where the animal isn't treated as a patient. Given the significant costs and the clinical quality that exists, one expects an organization to support it.
I'm a terrible center.

This review concerns only Nurse Eleonora and not the rest of the center's staff.

First of all, I would like to thank Martina, who welcomed me at the desk with great kindness and professionalism, and Dr. Martina Confaloni, who examined my kitten with expertise, empathy, and availability. The rest of the staff has always been knowledgeable and attentive.

Unfortunately, I cannot say the same for Nurse Eleonora. While I recognize her professional competence, her way of interacting with pet owners is, in my opinion, unacceptable. During my experience, she exhibited an aggressive and intimidating attitude: she stood too close to the faces of those she spoke to, raised her voice, and addressed people in a tone that I found offensive and disrespectful.

Anyone who visits a veterinary center already does so with great concern for their pet and deserves to be treated with respect and empathy.

It's a real shame, because someone with this attitude risks overshadowing the excellent work done by all the other professionals at the center. For this very reason, while I continue to have faith in the facility, I would feel uncomfortable if my cat were to be entrusted to its care again during a possible hospitalization.

I hope this report is taken as a constructive feedback, because the center truly deserves to maintain the high professional and humane standards that the rest of the staff demonstrates every day.

Excellent veterinary center. The doctor who examined my guinea pig was very kind, professional, and available to answer all my questions. She immediately identified the mite problem and prescribed the appropriate treatment. I had a great experience, highly recommended!
The staff is professional and very friendly. I would definitely recommend this facility for pet care.
Peaceful environment, very competent and friendly staff, ample parking

I would like to thank the medical and administrative staff at CVS Nomentano again for what they did for my boxer Teo. Teo was admitted to the facility in a truly dire condition for a nasty grass awn. All the staff (I repeat: administrative, nursing, and medical), in addition to being extremely professional, demonstrated rare empathy and courtesy! A special thanks to Dr. Zeyen, Dr. De Dominicis, and Dr. Zeyen.
The facility is clean, new, and very well-maintained.

On July 25th, we brought in an exotic parrot we found on the ground while we were on our way to a restaurant to celebrate my birthday! The bird couldn't fly and was bleeding from its nose. When we arrived at the emergency veterinary clinic, we were helped by Dr. Bassi, who was very kind and competent. She provided first aid, telling us later that it wasn't anything serious but had just taken a knock with a slight head injury! We paid for the visit and first aid and left! The next day, she sent us a video where we could see the parrot doing better, and within a few days, it will be taken to Rieti and then released back into the wild.
A place where you enter worried and leave calmer.

First and last time I've set foot here. A friend of mine finds an injured seagull, and we're considering other options besides the LIPU (Italian League for Bird Protection) (even if they charge a fee). This veterinary practice was recommended to us. Given its remote location—before crossing to Rome—I called them at 10 a.m. on July 24th to ask if they take in seagulls. After a short wait, they said yes, and confirmed that they also take care of releasing them into the wild. I told them we couldn't be there before 7-8 p.m. that same day, and they pointed out that the Emergency Room is open even at that time. We arrived at this practice with its narrow entrance just before 8 p.m., and told the receptionist about the seagull needing treatment. She replied that they don't take in seagulls. I pointed out that my colleague had told me on the phone that morning that they did take in seagulls. I was told that her colleague had obviously made a mistake. So much for the mistake, and congratulations on your professionalism! But what does it take to inform the staff that certain animals aren't being taken in? What do you have to do to get accurate information from this study? Call several times at different times and make sure they always give the same answer to a given question?! I've never been here before, and in all honesty, after a business card like that, I'll be wary of setting foot in there again for the rest of my life...
Excellent facility, both professional and friendly.

A brief and very painful experience, which ended with the death of our kitten. Dr. Ciavatta was an excellent veterinarian and also a shoulder I could cry on.
Not everyone. Uncommon in terms of empathy.
Courtesy and competence.
I have no complaints about the doctors' professionalism. But for 3 days, they NEVER answered the phone at any time!!!! It's a disgrace!
I've known Dr. Zeien for a long time and he's number one...
Professionals, punctuality and kindness

Super center, very empathetic staff, except for one girl with long hair and blue eyes.
I took time off work to go pick up the ashes of "my love," and she rudely told me you'd have to go during the day, unaware that I'd called three times with no answer and had stopped by twice the day before... SHE'S NOT THE ONLY ONE WORKING! Otherwise, I'll give her 2,000 stars 😊
Unfortunately, the emergency was traumatic, but we were welcomed with kindness, sensitivity, and a lot of empathy. Thank you so much, doctor!
Very professional veterinarians with various specializations

An excellent medical team saved my little bunny, who was in danger of climbing onto the bridge due to a blockage.
I have to say they're a bit expensive, but it's a sacrifice you have to make.

The CVS is truly a "safe place."
My kitten, "Sibir," is undergoing the examination peacefully thanks to the patience, professionalism, and expertise of all the medical staff.
Especially Dr. Liberati, whom he even kisses with his tongue.
Thank you!

We arrived on a Saturday in mid-July. Rome was deserted. Even the veterinary clinic was rotating hay bales in true Wild West style. A young veterinarian, specializing in neurology, handled the situation with grace and skill, despite the somewhat harsh attacks from anxious and aggressive owners, like this writer. A neurological examination and then an MRI scan ruled out the (certainly for us) nightmare of subsequent surgery. We waited a bit for reinforcements (radiologist and anesthesiologist) to arrive, but then everything went smoothly. Bravo!

Terrible!!! After checking in my elderly and infirm dog, they ALL disappeared for HOURS, both the secretaries and the doctors, leaving us there waiting. There was no one to ask for information, no one to tell you when the dog, who couldn't stand, would be seen, nothing at all. We waited the entire evening in vain, with no one bothering to show up. The same situation for other people with their pets who were there waiting. In the end, we had to leave without even being able to speak to anyone or have the examination! Total disregard, neglect, and rudeness towards customers. Avoid like the plague, never again!!!
Everything perfect
Very good, professional and very kind, very happy, my rabbit a little less, but it's in his nature.
Excellent structure and qualified staff

A few days ago, my husband brought our cat for an appointment. He arrived 10 minutes early and checked in, but couldn't wait inside because it was overcrowded. Outside, in the current heat, the cat began breathing heavily. After more than 20 minutes past the scheduled time and with the cat breathing through her mouth, my husband raised the issue but was told he'd have to wait another 20 minutes. At that point, he decided to leave. You decide for yourself whether this is the right course of action. We certainly won't be returning to this center, regardless of the quality of its doctors.
I found excellent professionals, a thorough examination and great empathy with my dog

My 14-year-old dog wasn't feeling well. We rushed to the CVS emergency room. We found professionalism and expertise, kindness, smiles, patience in providing answers, understanding. Flexible payment methods. I can only say I'm super satisfied. I extend my sincerest compliments to the director and all the staff for the excellent service provided by this facility. Everything was top-notch. Thank you so much, God bless you. P.S. At night, when I was being discharged, I had a question, so I called and emailed them with photos for them to review. They reassured me in the middle of the night by answering both the phone and email. What more can I say!? ❤️😊👍🙏😘

We came from another veterinary clinic closer to us "we arrived with an emergency" we were looked after by all the courteous, qualified, helpful staff "the only waiting time was at registration" there should be more people. My comment is disinterested because I did not know and do not know anyone from the facility.
Good, scrupulous, kind. A sure thing.

I waited a few days before writing. I'm doing so solely to share my experience and offer a perspective that may help you be very careful when choosing this facility.

Below is a summary of the facts.

I had a kitten of about 4 months who had been panting for a few days. On Monday, June 22, 2026, my wife took him to the emergency room of this clinic.

An X-ray was performed, and the kitten's lungs were found to be compromised. We were advised to administer a "pipette antiparasitic, as it is almost certainly a case of parasites that have invaded the lungs."

We were advised to have fecal tests, but unfortunately, since we don't have much money, we chose to proceed as recommended by the doctor on duty (€105, invoice received by email but no report or X-rays), trusting her opinion.

We were told that the kitten might worsen after the medication was administered and recommended a day hospital stay with them, which we agreed to do (cost €95, invoice received but no report).

Upon discharge, we were told to refill the antiparasitic pipette in 30 days, but were given no further instructions or treatment.

The kitten's condition worsened. During the night between June 24th and 25th, 2026, his agony became excruciating. We called them and were advised of the possibility of undergoing oxygen therapy there (total €150 per day). We also consulted two other veterinarians outside the clinic, but they advised us to return to the clinic for oxygen therapy.

Unfortunately (as a father of two children and a rent-paying bill), my financial resources were too low to cover these expenses. We sought advice on what to do, but received none.

At 5:30 a.m. on June 25, 2026, the kitten was dying. I rushed him to the clinic's emergency room. Two young doctors attempted resuscitation, but I asked them not to cause him any further suffering, and the poor thing died.

When I told them, "You gave him back to us in serious condition without providing any treatment or real advice, and no one even came forward to put an end to his possible agony," the doctor replied (among other sad things, but I'll summarize) in a pedantic manner, "Animals have become luxury goods. If you can't afford them, don't take them." I made it very clear that I felt this was all unfair and inconsistent with the profession one has chosen.

The next day, I emailed them to request the X-ray reports and to write in detail about what had happened. No response.

I call the office with the same request. The secretary (the only kind and understanding person I've ever dealt with there) is having trouble finding the report. She tells me she'll call me back. But nothing happens.

I send a certified email to the attention of management. Dr. Selleri calls and invites me to explain what happened over the phone. He tells me he's very sorry and will send me all the documentation.

The documents don't arrive. I invite the doctor via WhatsApp to send me the report and the x-rays. The doctor sends me a WhatsApp message with a summary of "what happened," written by him on the spot, pretending to be the report.

The next day, I ask for x-rays again. They finally arrive by email (still without any report).

I call the office again to request the report. The secretary tries to find it, but it's still missing.

That's it as of June 28, 2026.

I'm considering pursuing other avenues, but with the sole aim of not remaining silent in the face of a blatant case of injustice.

What deeply pains me (I've always had well-cared-for animals, and this is the first time I've found myself in a situation like this):
- the fate of the poor kitten
- no veterinarian in this story has been able to intervene to at least alleviate his suffering
- that I'm being mocked in this way when I'm requesting documents that are my right and their duty to provide.
